when guest MPX disabled"")
column2: KVM has taken ownership of the ""load

column1: IA32_BNDCFGS"" and ""clear IA32_BNDCFGS"" VMX entry/exit controls
trying to set these bits in the IA32_VMX_TRUE_{ENTRY
MSRs if the guest's CPUID supports MPX
The intent of the patch was to apply it to L0 in order to work around
L1 kernels that lack the fix in commit 691bd4340bef (""kvm: vmx: allow
host to access guest MSR_IA32_BNDCFGS""
control bits from L0
and the L1 bug is neutralized even in the lack of commit 691bd4340bef.
This was perhaps a sensible kludge at the time
idea in the long term and in fact it has not been extended to
other CPUID bits like these:
X86_FEATURE_LM => VM_EXIT_HOST_ADDR_SPACE_SIZE
VMX_MISC_SAVE_EFER_LMA
X86_FEATURE_TSC => CPU_BASED_RDTSC_EXITING
SECONDARY_EXEC_TSC_SCALING
X86_FEATURE_INVPCID_SINGLE => SECONDARY_EXEC_ENABLE_INVPCID
X86_FEATURE_MWAIT => CPU_BASED_MONITOR_EXITING
X86_FEATURE_INTEL_PT => SECONDARY_EXEC_PT_CONCEAL_VMX
VM_EXIT_CLEAR_IA32_RTIT_CTL
X86_FEATURE_XSAVES => SECONDARY_EXEC_XSAVES
These days it's sort of common knowledge that any MSR in
KVM_GET_MSR_INDEX_LIST must allow *at least* setting it with KVM_SET_MSR
to a default value
